name: fix_makefile_incremental_rebuild
description: Fixes a Makefile rule with no prerequisites that never rebuilds
prompts: The Makefile builds `app` from calc.c and main.c, but the `app` target lists NO prerequisites - so after the first build, editing calc.c doesn't trigger a rebuild (make sees `app` exists and stops). Fix the Makefile so `app` depends on calc.c and main.c and is rebuilt whenever either changes. Keep the executable name `app` and the clean target. Recipe lines stay tab-indented.

setup_files.Makefile:
CC = gcc

# BUG: the `app` rule has NO prerequisites, so once app exists make thinks it
# is up to date and never recompiles when calc.c changes.
app:
	$(CC) -o app calc.c main.c

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app

test_setup_files.test_rebuild.py:
import os, subprocess, time

def make(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['make', *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45)

r = make()
assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
out = subprocess.run(['./app'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout.strip()
assert out == '1', f'initial build should print 1, got {out!r}'

# change calc.c; make must rebuild and the new behavior must show
time.sleep(1.1)  # ensure a strictly newer mtime for make's comparison
with open('calc.c', 'w') as f:
    f.write('int compute(void) { return 42; }\n')

r = make()
assert r.returncode == 0, f'rebuild failed: {r.stderr}'
out = subprocess.run(['./app'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout.strip()
assert out == '42', f'make did NOT rebuild after calc.c changed (still prints {out!r})'

# no spurious rebuild when nothing changed
r = make()
assert 'up to date' in (r.stdout + r.stderr).lower() or r.returncode == 0
print('PASS')

reference_solution.Makefile:
CC = gcc

app: calc.c main.c
	$(CC) -o app calc.c main.c

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app

files.Makefile:
CC = gcc

app: main.c
	$(CC) -o app calc.c main.c

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -f app
